core.title: Near Optimal Bayesian Active Learning for Decision Making
core.publication_status: AISTATS 2014 PMLR 33:430-438, identity visible in cached proceedings paper
core.reading_this_branch: Focused primary reread PDF pages 1-4 and 8. Did not rerun HEC or claim to read the entire proof/implementation pages 5-7.
core.problem: Choose costly tests until all surviving hypotheses fall within one overlapping action-success decision region.
core.mechanism: Construct a splitting hypergraph; greedily maximize expected cut weight until no incompatible cross-region hyperedge survives.
core.benchmark_and_protocol: MovieLens comparison-based learning and simulated button-pushing localization; read robot section reports 10 environments times 100 hypotheses and 150 guarded candidate tests.
core.result: In the read robot experiment HEC and myopic VoI are essentially alike over short horizons; this is not evidence of universal superiority.
core.limits: Finite hypotheses with a prior and deterministic test outcomes; exponential dependence on hyperedge cardinality. Its theorem does not certify this continuous source solver or noisy proxy.
core.local_transfer: R1 reuses an existing cost-of-next-action gate for known channels while scanning stations; not a reimplementation of HEC. Unknown channels are measured normally.
core.local_evidence: R1 retained on 4800 exposed cases, but this is an engineering transfer and paired policy result, not a causal attribution to the paper.

core.title: Adaptive Submodular Ranking and Routing
core.publication_status: Read arXiv:1606.01530v2, 5 February 2019; journal identity from older registry not needed for this branch's claims
core.reading_this_branch: Focused primary reread PDF pages 1-3, 6-7, 22-25. Not a full proof audit of the routing theorem.
core.problem: Adaptively cover an unknown scenario from a known distribution with scenario-specific monotone submodular completion functions.
core.mechanism: ASR combines probability of informative scenario elimination with relative completion gain, divided by test cost; ASP extends the framing to metric routing.
core.benchmark_and_protocol: ODT and threshold ODT on 10 WISER variants (415 chemicals, 79 binary symptoms with unknown entries randomly completed), plus constructed hard instances; costs are unit tests.
core.result: ASR and Greedy are close and neither dominates WISER; constructed hard examples favor ASR. The read experiments are not physical robot-route experiments.
core.limits: Known finite scenario distribution, feedback and submodular completion structure are not established for this hidden-source environment. No approximation bound is transferred.
core.local_transfer: R2 interrupts one localization round at a natural boundary and replans the original global route. R3-R5 test cost/information proxies; they are not ASR/ASP implementations.
core.local_evidence: R2 retained; R3-R5 all regressed in quick and D2 stopped after three nonpromotions. This diagnoses the tested proxies, not adaptive planning as a whole.
classification: Separate information and completion progress per cost

core.title: Coverage control for mobile sensing networks
core.publication_status: Read arXiv:math/0212212v1, 16 December 2002; no later-version identity or convergence claim inferred
core.reading_this_branch: Focused primary reading of section III-C and its references 44-46; not the whole paper and not its full simulation section.
core.problem: Worst-case distance coverage when no density model is available, distinct from expected-distance p-median coverage.
core.mechanism: Rewrite the maximum nearest-site distance as the maximum over Voronoi cells, and move each site toward its cell's minimum enclosing sphere center.
core.benchmark_and_protocol: No paper simulation result adopted; the read III-C subsection supplies a geometric decomposition and suggests a p-center algorithm.
core.result: The inspected version explicitly does not provide a convergence proof for the discussed p-center algorithm there. No global optimality claim is made.
core.limits: Our fixed visited sites, fixed paid anchor, four finite updates, and station-route guard are additional engineering choices. They are not this paper's distributed controller or a convergence theorem.
core.local_transfer: R8 uses constrained minimax relocation only to propose future sites; original continuous cover certificate is still required. R9 tests adding it after R7 rotation proposals fail.
core.local_evidence: R8 full 4800 complete but two exposed batches disagree against R7; not retained. R6 certificate predates this reading and must not be retrospectively credited to the paper.
classification: Worst-case Voronoi radius and minimax site relocation
